A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DiscoGen/DiscoBench work and provide readable main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices. Reordered sections and previously documented capabilities can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original DiscoBench evaluations of three LLM-backed agents, prompt-tuning experiments, module-combination analyses, and discovered algorithms.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and reports expanded domain evaluations, held-out-domain prompt performance, and an initialization ablation.

M1.justification: The task generator, two-stage meta-train/meta-test construction, MLGym scaffold, and Claude/DeepSeek prompt-tuning procedure remain unchanged. The additional domains and on-policy target/activation modules emphasized in v2 were already specified in v1 Appendices B–C.

E1.justification: Evaluated coverage expands from ten to fourteen domains, adding neural cellular automata, offline RL, on-policy MARL, and trajectory prediction. These were described but not evaluated in v1. v2 includes their DiscoBench results and uses them for explicitly held-out-domain prompt evaluation.

E2.justification: The three LLM-backed agents and all-fixed DiscoBench baseline are retained. However, v2 Appendix J.9–J.10 adds all-fixed baseline references to per-task comparisons of tuned prompts; v1's corresponding prompt-tuning results compared the four task-count conditions without that reference.

E3.justification: v2 adds evaluation on four domains outside the retained ten-domain prompt-training distribution. The module sweep expands from 15 configurations of four modules to 63 configurations of six modules. The new initialization experiment controls starting code across eight selected domains using DeepSeek-v3.2. Existing benchmark action budgets and dataset splits are retained.

E4.justification: Section 8.2 adds an empty-versus-baseline initialization ablation and qualitative examination of resulting algorithms. Section 8.1 substantially expands v1 Appendix G's module sweep, while dropping its detailed maximum-score summary. Section 7 adds an explicit analysis of generalization beyond the prompt-training domain distribution.

E5.justification: Both versions specify three meta-seeds, additional attempts until three successful runs where feasible, and 95% Elo intervals from 100 bootstrap rounds. Per-task stratified bootstrap intervals and interquartile means are retained, as are eight-inner-seed means and standard errors for the single-task prompt-tuning curves.

E6.justification: Benchmark aggregates, success@3 values, and numerous per-task results change. For example, DeepSeek's Single-Edit success rate changes from 80.0% in v1 Table 2 to 71.3% in v2 Table 3 on expanded coverage, not a comparable-setting decline. New results include held-out-domain prompt scores and initialization success rates of 92.4% versus 75.4% in Section 8.2.

T1.justification: The task-count formula, its inclusion-exclusion derivation, the model-unlearning extension, and Elo equations are unchanged between v1 Appendices E–F and v2 Appendices C–D. No new theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The generator and benchmark contributions remain central. The introduction and conclusion extend the prompt-optimization claim to domains outside the optimization distribution and explicitly emphasize validation of task-difficulty controls. The advertised billions-scale task space was already documented in v1 Appendix C.

C2.justification: For the revised benchmark, v2 replaces v1's strong All-Edit model-ranking statement with caution about low success rates. It interprets baseline initialization as easier but liable to preserve the initial implementation, and explicitly identifies prompt-only optimization and limited model/scaffold coverage as remaining limitations.

D1.justification: v1 Appendix O's extensive domain, dataset, and module prompt specifications are removed and replaced by repository access guidance in v2 Appendix D.1. The documented five-task learned prompt also changes, without explaining whether this is a correction or a new run. v2 adds MARL's four-GPU requirement and updates estimated total compute from 23,000 to 35,000 GPU-hours.

R1.justification: v2 adds references to ProgramBench, Hyperagents, and process reward models, and presents benchmark positioning in a new property-comparison table. The underlying related-work argument remains stable; most other bibliographic revisions update publication metadata rather than introduce different works.

P1.justification: The document is substantially reorganized: design analyses gain a main-text section, domain appendices are consolidated, successful-run results move out of the main comparison, and the task-prompt appendix is removed. Method and research-direction passages are condensed, and evaluation terminology and section titles are revised.

P2.justification: v2 adds the benchmark-property table, restructures main result tables, replaces module-summary tables with Figure 2, and extensively expands appendix plots. Some presentation becomes less specific: many combination panels in Figures 32–39 use 'OnPolicyRL all' instead of v1's explicit module-combination labels.

improvement.justification: v1's empirical validation covered ten domains and pooled prompt-tuning performance. v2 evaluates the four previously untested domains, explicitly separates transfer beyond the training-domain distribution, and adds controlled initialization comparisons and broader module ablations. These address important gaps in validating diversity, generalization, and controllable difficulty. The gains outweigh reduced self-contained prompt documentation and less informative combination-plot labels.
